name: Suvarnadurg Fort
tagline: An island fort near Murud Beach, captured by Shivaji Maharaj in the 1660s
seoTitle: Suvarnadurg Fort Solo Guide — The Solo Trail
seoDescription: Solo traveler's guide to Suvarnadurg, a Konkan coast island sea fort near Ratnagiri's Murud Beach — boat access and safety notes.
dataNote: Boat-access island fort, not a hiking trek — part of Maharashtra's lighter-weight coastal/Konkan sea fort circuit.

seasons.label: Oct – Feb
seasons.sub: Calmest seas for the boat crossing

seasons.label: Jun – Sep
seasons.sub: Monsoon — rough seas can suspend crossings

routeOptions.name: Boat from Harnai jetty
routeOptions.duration: Short crossing + 1–2 hrs on the fort
routeOptions.notes: Captured by Shivaji Maharaj in the 1660s; a straightforward boat-and-walk visit, not a trek.

safety.intro: Same profile as Maharashtra's other island sea forts — sea conditions matter more than any walking difficulty.

cards.title: Before you go
items: Check with local boat operators about sea conditions before traveling
This fort is less touristed than Janjira — confirm boat availability in advance

cards.title: On the trail
items: Uneven weathered stone inside the fort — mind your footing
Limited facilities — carry water and snacks

cards.title: Solo-specific
items: Quieter than Janjira — confirm you'll have a boat operator willing to make the crossing for a solo traveler, or coordinate with others
Safe destination overall, mainly a logistics consideration

gettingThere.intro: There is no ferry service here — the crossing is an informal arrangement with Harnai's fishermen.

steps.title: Reach Ratnagiri or Dapoli
steps.body: These have far better train and bus connectivity than Khed, the technically-nearest Konkan Railway station (still about 43 km from Harnai).

steps.title: Onward to Harnai
steps.body: ST buses or shared vehicles run from Ratnagiri or Dapoli to Harnai fishing harbour, roughly 1–1.5 hours.

steps.title: Arrange a boat with local fishermen at Harnai
steps.body: There is no scheduled ferry and no ticket counter — this is entirely a word-of-mouth arrangement with fishermen at the harbour. Go in the morning, be flexible on timing, and expect to negotiate.

steps.title: The crossing
steps.body: About 10–15 minutes each way, depending on tide, weather and the operator's willingness. Avoid monsoon season (roughly June–September) — seas are rough and fishermen generally won't take visitors out.

gettingThere.permitNote: No formal booking system exists for this crossing; it depends entirely on finding a willing local fisherman and calm seas. Build slack into your schedule and don't count on a same-day guarantee. Of all the treks on this site, this is the one most likely to simply not happen on the day you planned it.

transport.item: Overnight bus/train: Mumbai/Pune → Ratnagiri or Dapoli

onTrail.note: Per person if joining others; ₹1,500–2,500 for a full small boat solo
